title: Codex CLI 0.150.1 fixes Remote compaction image budgeting
author: OpenAI / Codex changelog
why_it_matters: Remote compaction now counts retained images toward its token budget and trims older images as needed, making screenshot-heavy long sessions a real context-budget concern.
actionable_takeaway: Create a Context Payload Budget that tracks text, screenshots, image inputs and file excerpts before a long Codex run hits compaction failure.

title: Codex CLI 0.150.1 GitHub release
author: OpenAI / GitHub
why_it_matters: The public GitHub release confirms the 0.150.1 bug fix and links it to the retained-image compaction path, useful for reproducing and tracking upgrade status.
actionable_takeaway: When a remote Codex task has images, record local CLI version, compaction behavior, and whether retained images were summarized or kept.

title: Work with more websites in ChatGPT Work and Codex
author: OpenAI / ChatGPT Learn
why_it_matters: The weekly digest separates local browser use, Site tools(WebMCP), and cloud browser sign-in, each with different permission and evidence boundaries.
actionable_takeaway: Before any website task, declare the browser lane, allowed actions, readback method, and stop conditions instead of saying only 'use browser'.

title: Site tools(WebMCP) expose website actions to agents
author: OpenAI / ChatGPT Learn
why_it_matters: Site tools let ChatGPT Work and Codex use structured actions offered by websites in the built-in browser, reducing fragile pixel-level UI automation.
actionable_takeaway: For internal tools, draft an Agent Tool Surface Spec with action names, input schema, result schema, permissions, dry-run and audit fields.

title: Cloud browser sign-in is a separate account lane
author: OpenAI / ChatGPT Learn
why_it_matters: Cloud browser sign-in supports account-needed tasks on eligible plans, but does not connect the user's local browser profile and must use a dedicated sign-in flow.
actionable_takeaway: Never put credentials in chat; route sign-in through the browser flow and record that cloud-browser evidence is separate from local-browser evidence.

title: Scheduled tasks can respond to Gmail, Slack, and GitHub events
author: OpenAI Help Center
why_it_matters: Scheduled tasks can now respond to connected-app updates and be shared in a workspace, moving personal automation from fixed cron to event-triggered operations.
actionable_takeaway: Write a Trigger Envelope for every event task: source app, payload schema, idempotency key, owner, connector permissions, artifact and duplicate handling.

title: Premium seats change capacity planning for ChatGPT Business and Codex
author: OpenAI Help Center
why_it_matters: Premium seats give high-usage teammates more capacity, remove five-hour usage limits, and keep centralized billing and spend controls.
actionable_takeaway: Separate seat entitlement from run budget: record who needs Premium capacity, which workflows justify it, and what per-run spend gate still applies.

title: Computer History turns Mac activity into opt-in memories
author: OpenAI / ChatGPT Learn
why_it_matters: Computer History lets ChatGPT and Codex reference selected activity across apps and websites, but is off by default and controlled by user/admin choice.
actionable_takeaway: Create a Computer History Boundary Card: allowed apps/sites, pause/delete policy, sensitive exclusions, and when the timeline cannot be used for public output.

title: Record & Replay converts stable desktop workflows into skills
author: OpenAI / ChatGPT Learn
why_it_matters: Record & Replay can turn demonstrated macOS workflows into reusable skills that later run with Computer Use, browser actions, or plugins.
actionable_takeaway: Only record stable workflows with clear success criteria; scrub unrelated windows first and verify the generated skill's inputs, stops and readback steps.

title: Plugins package skills, connectors, MCP servers, hooks, and task templates
author: OpenAI / ChatGPT Learn
why_it_matters: Plugins are becoming reusable workflow bundles shared across ChatGPT and Codex surfaces, not just one-off extensions.
actionable_takeaway: Maintain a Plugin Capability Inventory that lists skills, connectors, MCP servers, hooks, scheduled templates, write actions and required account connections.

title: Plugin-bundled MCP servers need explicit tool policy
author: OpenAI / ChatGPT Learn
why_it_matters: Installed plugins can bundle MCP servers, and user config can control on/off state and tool policy under the plugin's MCP server path.
actionable_takeaway: For every plugin-provided MCP server, record enabled_tools, disabled_tools, default_tools_approval_mode and per-tool approval rules.

title: Configuration reference exposes per-plugin MCP approval controls
author: OpenAI / ChatGPT Learn
why_it_matters: The config reference defines plugin MCP approval modes and allow/deny tool lists, giving teams a concrete schema for least-privilege tool access.
actionable_takeaway: Use a Plugin/MCP Approval Matrix before enabling new tools: read/search auto, write prompt, send/publish approve-once, unknown disabled.

title: GitHub Copilot enterprise managed settings support multiple deployment paths
author: GitHub Docs
why_it_matters: Enterprise managed settings can be deployed server-side, through MDM, or by file, with different timing and client coverage for Copilot agent guardrails.
actionable_takeaway: Build a Managed AI Settings Runbook that records default config, team overrides, delivery path, supported clients and verification steps.

title: Enterprise managed settings reference documents bypass and permission controls
author: GitHub Docs
why_it_matters: The reference shows how bypass or allow-all behavior can be disabled and how settings vary by client, which matters for agent safety baselines.
actionable_takeaway: Do not assume every client supports every permission key; keep a client support matrix for bypass, allow, ask, deny, model, plugins and MCP settings.

title: VS Code explains AI settings precedence across MDM, server and file channels
author: Visual Studio Code Docs
why_it_matters: VS Code documents per-key precedence across native MDM, server-managed and file-based settings, plus interaction with VS Code enterprise policies.
actionable_takeaway: When debugging AI policy drift, read back all three channels and decide which single channel should own each key instead of expecting merges.

title: Codex GitHub Action runs Codex in workflows with a secure proxy
author: OpenAI / GitHub
why_it_matters: The action shows Codex moving into CI workflows while keeping control over available privileges and API access paths.
actionable_takeaway: Treat CI Codex runs as production automations: pin workflow permissions, proxy/API access, artifacts, review gates and rollback evidence.

title: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.22.0 hardens guardrails, failed status handling and usage isolation
author: OpenAI / GitHub
why_it_matters: The release redacts blocked tool outputs from replay state, raises errors for terminal failed/incomplete responses, and isolates usage accounting between checkpoints.
actionable_takeaway: Update agent test fixtures to assert redaction, terminal failure handling, checkpoint usage isolation and nested-agent aggregation before upgrading SDK versions.
